_doc: data/protocol_safety.json — the STRUCTURED promotion of two things the protocol pages already say
in prose, and a build gate that keeps the promotion honest.
Measured hydrated at 390x844 on all 52 /protocol/* routes before this file existed:
· a labelled stop-rule element:            0 of 52
· a named primary tracking metric element: 0 of 52
· the 🚩 reassess block AFTER the first supplement recommendation: 52 of 52
(the prose versions were there — .plan-working 52/52 and .plan-reassess 52/52 — but as paragraphs,
so nothing on the page named ONE number to track or ONE point at which the answer is to stop.)
Shape: problem id -> { metric, metricSource, checkpoint, stopIssue }.
metric       a short label. PROMOTION ONLY — written with words the problem's own `working`
prose already uses. assertProtocolSafety() in build/parse.js rejects any label word
(4+ characters, minus a small function-word list) that does not appear in that prose.
metricSource the exact sentence the label was promoted from. Must be a VERBATIM substring of
data/protocol_plan.json[id].working. It is printed under the label on the page, so a
reader always sees the authored sentence, not only the condensation.
checkpoint   the `when` of the problem's own honest-checkpoint timeline rung (the last one).
Must match a `when` that timeline actually contains, verbatim.
stopIssue    which authored troubleshooting entry IS the stop rule. Must match an existing
`issue` verbatim; the page renders that entry's authored `fix` as the action.
So no sentence on the page is written here: this file SELECTS authored text and gives it a name.
Nothing here was reviewed by a clinician or any other authoritative professional, and nothing in it
may be presented as reviewed by a person. It is an editorial promotion of an authored text corpus.

acne.metric: New inflamed spots, counted week over week
acne.metricSource: Fewer *new* inflamed spots week over week (count them — memory lies)
acne.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of a consistent regimen

knee-pain.metric: Pain on stairs, kneeling and standing up, week over week
knee-pain.metricSource: Less pain on stairs, kneeling, and standing up after sitting — the everyday moments, not just gym days.
knee-pain.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of consistent strengthening

low-back-pain.metric: How long you can sit, stand and walk before the ache builds
low-back-pain.metricSource: You can sit, stand, and walk for longer before the ache builds
low-back-pain.stopIssue: No real change after 6–8 weeks of consistent movement and loading

neck-shoulder.metric: Longer to tighten, faster to let go
neck-shoulder.metricSource: Your neck and shoulders take **longer to tighten** through the day and **let go faster** after a reset break
neck-shoulder.stopIssue: No real change after 6 to 8 weeks of consistent work

hip-mobility.metric: Flare-ups per week, and how long you can lie on the painful side
hip-mobility.metricSource: how long you can lie on the painful side before it aches, how many flare-ups you get in a week
hip-mobility.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of consistent strengthening

elbow-wrist.metric: Pain during the session and the morning after, and the weights and reps
elbow-wrist.metricSource: less pain during the session and the morning after**, and you can gradually **handle more load or grip before it complains** — track the actual weights and reps
elbow-wrist.stopIssue: No improvement after about 12 weeks of consistent loading

ankle-foot.metric: Morning first-step ache 0–10, and how far you walked
ankle-foot.metricSource: how far you walked, how many calf raises, how bad the morning stiffness was on a 0–10 scale
ankle-foot.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of consistent loading

sarcopenia.metric: Lifting more than a month ago, grip and balance
sarcopenia.metricSource: You're lifting more than you could a month ago, and daily tasks — stairs, carrying shopping, rising from a low chair — feel easier. Grip and balance improve
sarcopenia.stopIssue: No strength gain after 8-12 weeks of consistent training

insulin-resistance.metric: Fasting number and after-meal spikes, over weeks
insulin-resistance.metricSource: after-meal spikes that are lower and settle faster**, with your fasting number drifting down over weeks
insulin-resistance.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of a consistent routine

visceral-fat.metric: Waist measurement at the navel, once a month
visceral-fat.metricSource: A **falling waist measurement** (measure at your navel, same time of day, once a month — memory and the mirror both lie)
visceral-fat.stopIssue: No change in waist after 12 consistent weeks

chronic-fatigue.metric: Energy out of ten, each morning and mid-afternoon
chronic-fatigue.metricSource: rate your energy out of ten each morning and mid-afternoon for a couple of weeks
chronic-fatigue.stopIssue: Two weeks of genuinely good sleep and I'm still wiped out

cravings.metric: Cravings on a normal day — fewer and weaker
cravings.metricSource: Fewer and weaker cravings on a normal day — you can walk past the snack cupboard without a fight
cravings.stopIssue: No real change after 4–6 weeks of a consistent protein-and-fiber base

thyroid.metric: TSH, free T3 and ferritin on retest — and how you feel week to week
thyroid.metricSource: On retest the trend is what matters — TSH settling, free T3 rising, ferritin climbing back up
thyroid.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of eating enough and fixing cofactors

blood-pressure.metric: The 7-day average systolic on your home cuff
blood-pressure.metricSource: A falling **7-day average** on your home cuff — not one lucky reading — is the real sign, especially the top (**systolic**) number easing down
blood-pressure.stopIssue: No meaningful change after 6–8 weeks of genuinely doing the diet and lifestyle changes

cholesterol.metric: LDL on a repeat blood test, with triglycerides and HDL
cholesterol.metricSource: the only honest scoreboard is a **repeat blood test**, so compare the actual numbers, not how virtuous you feel. Progress looks like a falling **LDL** (the harmful cholesterol), falling **triglycerides** (blood fat that sugar and alcohol drive up), and a slowly rising **HDL** (the protective kind)
cholesterol.stopIssue: LDL barely moved after 12 weeks of genuine diet change

brain-fog.metric: Fog 0–10 each night, with your wake time and sleep hours
brain-fog.metricSource: each night, rate your fog 0–10 and note your wake time and rough sleep hours
brain-fog.stopIssue: Sleep is genuinely fixed but the fog hasn't lifted after 6–8 weeks

anxiety.metric: Anxiety surges, and a 0-to-10 rating each evening
anxiety.metricSource: fewer and shorter **anxiety surges** week over week, a lower background hum of dread, and being able to actually *switch off* when you rest rather than lying there wired. Track it simply — a 0-to-10 rating each evening
anxiety.stopIssue: No change after 6 weeks of consistent effort

low-mood.metric: Mood once a day, a simple 1-to-10 score
low-mood.metricSource: Track your **mood once a day** with a simple 1-to-10 score and note what you did
low-mood.stopIssue: No change after 6–8 weeks of doing the routine consistently

adhd-focus.metricSource: how many focused blocks you complete a day
adhd-focus.stopIssue: No change after 8–12 weeks of consistent sleep, food and structure

memory.metric: A one-line daily note on word-finding and what sticks
memory.metricSource: when word-finding feels quicker, when new names, plans and where-you-put-things stick more reliably, and when the heavy mid-afternoon fog lifts — most of all on well-slept days. Track it simply, since a one-line daily note
memory.stopIssue: No change after two to three months of fixing sleep and the basics

burnout.metric: A 1-to-10 energy and mood score each morning
burnout.metricSource: a 1-to-10 energy and mood score each morning beats memory, which always rounds toward
burnout.stopIssue: No improvement after 3–4 weeks of genuinely protected rest

insomnia.metric: How long lights-out to asleep takes, week over week
insomnia.metricSource: You fall asleep a little **faster week over week** — track roughly how long lights-out to asleep takes, since memory tends to exaggerate the bad nights
insomnia.stopIssue: No change after 3–4 weeks of a consistent routine

sleep-maintenance.metric: Nights waking, and how fast you fall back asleep
sleep-maintenance.metricSource: **fewer nights waking** and, on the nights you do wake, you **fall back asleep faster** instead of lying there for an hour — jot it down briefly each morning
sleep-maintenance.stopIssue: No change after 4–6 weeks of a genuinely consistent routine

shift-work.metric: Sleep and wake times, and a 1-to-10 alertness score each day
shift-work.metricSource: jot down your actual sleep and wake times and a 1-to-10 alertness score each day
shift-work.stopIssue: Two-plus weeks in and nothing has shifted

low-testosterone.metric: Morning erections and libido, with two morning readings on retest
low-testosterone.metricSource: Returning **morning erections** and steadier libido, **energy that holds through the afternoon**, easier recovery from training, and mood and motivation lifting week over week — these day-to-day signs usually move *before* the blood number does. When you retest, look for a genuine upward trend across two morning readings rather than one lucky result
low-testosterone.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of honest lifestyle effort

menopause.metric: A rough flush count and a sleep note, week to week
menopause.metricSource: Track it simply week to week (a rough flush count and a sleep note beat memory)
menopause.stopIssue: Still getting flushes or poor sleep after 8–12 weeks on HRT

low-libido.metric: Desire showing up on its own, tracked over weeks
low-libido.metricSource: Desire showing up **on its own** — a passing thought, morning arousal, reaching for your partner without having to manufacture it — rather than something you have to force. Track the trend over weeks
low-libido.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of genuinely better sleep and lower stress

bone-density.metric: Lifting heavier month over month, and your DXA scan
bone-density.metricSource: You're lifting **noticeably heavier** month over month, you feel **steadier on your feet** with fewer trips and wobbles, and if your vitamin D or protein was low, those have been corrected. Over the long run, "working" means a **stable or improved DXA scan
bone-density.stopIssue: A repeat DXA scan shows no improvement after 1-2 years

pcos.metric: Waist measurement, cycle-start dates and training weights
pcos.metricSource: Track a couple of concrete things (a waist measurement, your cycle-start dates, your training weights)
pcos.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of consistent food and training

skin-aging.metric: Photos in the same light and angle, every month
skin-aging.metricSource: Track it with **photos in the same light and angle every month**

hair-loss.metric: Hairs you lose in the shower or on the pillow, across a week
hair-loss.metricSource: Fewer hairs coming out day to day — try counting what you lose in the shower or on the pillow across a week
hair-loss.stopIssue: No visible change after 6 months of consistent treatment

longevity.metric: Easy-cardio pace at the same effort, and your waist
longevity.metricSource: your easy-cardio pace improves at the same effort, you can lift or carry a bit more than a month ago, your waist shrinks even when the scale is stubborn
longevity.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of honest, consistent effort

inflammation.metric: Energy, bloating and joint stiffness weekly — and CRP if bloods are run
inflammation.metricSource: steadier energy through the day with fewer afternoon crashes, less bloating and joint stiffness, and faster recovery between workouts — track these weekly
inflammation.stopIssue: No real change after 12 weeks of consistent effort

gut-health.metric: Plant-type count, and stools regular and easier to pass
gut-health.metricSource: stools that are **more regular and easier to pass** (not racing to the toilet, not straining), and a widening range of foods you can eat without a reaction. A useful marker is the **plant-type count** creeping up week over week
gut-health.stopIssue: No change after 12 weeks of a consistent routine

immunity.metric: Infections over a season — how often, how long
immunity.metricSource: Fewer infections over a season, and — just as important — the ones you do catch tend to be **milder and shorter** (a cold that clears in a few days instead of dragging on for weeks)
immunity.stopIssue: Still getting sick often after 12 weeks of good sleep and habits

hypertrophy.metric: Logbook trend — weight, reps and hard sets over a few weeks
hypertrophy.metricSource: Your **logbook trend is rising** — over a few weeks you're lifting more weight, getting more reps, or doing more hard sets than before
hypertrophy.stopIssue: I did everything and still nothing after 3+ months

strength-plateau.metric: Log trend — weight, reps or sets climbing week over week
strength-plateau.metricSource: Your **log trends up** — not every session, but week over week the weight, reps, or sets are climbing (write it down; memory flatters you)
strength-plateau.stopIssue: No change after 6–8 weeks of consistent training

fat-loss-plateau.metric: Weekly-average weight, and your waist measurement
fat-loss-plateau.metricSource: a **downward trend in your weekly-average weight**, not a lower number every single morning — day-to-day readings bounce with water, salt, sleep and hormones. Real progress also shows up off the scale: your **waist measurement creeping down**, clothes fitting looser
fat-loss-plateau.stopIssue: No change after 3–4 weeks of honest logging and holding your steps

endurance-plateau.metric: Easy pace at the same heart rate
endurance-plateau.metricSource: your **easy pace getting faster at the same heart rate**, or your heart rate dropping at a pace that used to feel hard
endurance-plateau.stopIssue: No change after a clean 4–6 week block and deload

pre-workout.metric: A 1-to-10 energy score in your training log
pre-workout.metricSource: a 1-to-10 energy score in your training log beats memory, which flatters the good days
pre-workout.stopIssue: No change after 3–4 weeks of eating, hydrating and sleeping well

overtraining.metric: Resting heart rate, first thing each morning
overtraining.metricSource: your **resting heart rate** (take it first thing each morning — memory lies, so write it down)
overtraining.stopIssue: No rebound after a full two-week deload with more food and sleep
